input: The performance of a mechanical-draft tower located at a chemical site was logged over the course of one summer month, in order to build up a picture of how the tower behaved under warm-season operating conditions. Over the period covered by the logging, the mean wet-bulb temperature was 25 °C, the approach was 4 K and the range was 8 K. It is important to appreciate, however, that the performance of the tower outside the month that was logged was not measured as part of this work, and this applies in particular to the performance the tower would deliver at the winter wet-bulb temperatures experienced at the site during the colder part of the year, for which no corresponding measurements are available in the material that has been gathered. The figures that are reported should consequently be read as describing the behaviour of the tower during the single month in which the logging took place, and they should not be taken as representing the behaviour of the tower across the year as a whole, since the conditions under which the tower operates are known to vary with the seasons even though the extent of that variation has not been captured here.
target: Performance of a mechanical-draft tower at a chemical site was logged over one summer month. Mean wet-bulb temperature was 25 °C, the approach was 4 K, and the range was 8 K. Performance outside the logged month was not measured, in particular at winter wet-bulb temperatures. The three reported values describe the tower under the wet-bulb conditions of that month. The approach is the difference the tower held between its cooled-water outlet temperature and the wet-bulb temperature of the entering air, and the range is the cooling the water underwent across the tower in the same period. Both are operating results for the logged conditions, not ratings for the year. A cooling tower works against the wet-bulb temperature of the air it draws in, and that temperature is at its highest in summer, so a summer month presents the tower with its most demanding common condition at the site. The logged month is in that sense a severe test. It is not, however, a complete one: the tower's behaviour in cold air, where the wet-bulb temperature falls and the cooling duty changes character, stands outside the measurement, and no winter figure can be read off from the summer record. The record also fixes the meaning of the two differences. The approach is measured against the wet-bulb temperature of the entering air, so it moves if that temperature moves; the range is measured on the water alone. A reader comparing towers must compare approach with approach at a stated wet-bulb temperature, not either value without its reference.
